ACCEPTThe internal-root barrier theorem is correct under the explicit full-original U/rotor model. The predecessor  $X_{j-1}$  bounds the incident depth in both U orientations; that bound eliminates every right E owner at an internal root. The eleven-point footprint, refined interval gap, phase inventory, and stated example of an endpoint-disjoint but nonextendible partial family all follow.There is one harmless terminology correction: in the predecessor segment, the row  $a_j-z_{j-1}+8$  is the bottommost row, meaning the largest row coordinate. It is above  $y_j$ , but it is not the segment’s topmost row. The proof uses the correct extremum, so its inequality and conclusions are unaffected.The argument obstructs cloning the first-root package at internal blocks. It does not contradict the accepted first-root theorem or conditional additivity for distinct additions with disjoint affected physical-tile footprints.1. Actual-owner normalization is justified for the complete originalsFix a block and write
$$a=a_j,\qquad C=C_j,\qquad y=(a-1,C).$$
The stated support and neighboring endpoints are correct: $y$  is the image of the canonical E support  $(5,6)$ . $(a-1,C-1)$  belongs to  $P_j$ , whose near column occupies every row of  $[a-8,a+2]$ . $(a,C)$  is the far terminal of  $E_j$ . $(a-1,C+1)$  belongs to the root when  $j=0$ , or to  $V_{j-1}$  when  $j>0$ .For an internal block, the predecessor V’s far column is
$$s_{j-1}+2=C_j+1,$$
and its full occupied row interval is
$$[a_{j-1}-6,\ a_{j-1}-6+z_{j-1}]
=[a_j-z_{j-1},\ a_j].$$
This includes the required east neighbor and the east-side collision points used later.The absence of  $y$  from H3 is consistent with the whole retained construction. In particular, the predecessor’s long V column lies one column to its right; the predecessor’s  $P,X,Z$  pieces that can reach its column end well above  $y$ ; still earlier blocks are separated by columns; and later blocks begin below it.Because  $y$  is an unconsumed original support with at least three occupied neighbors, completeness forces an actual original to contain it. That owner is fresh. Its matching neighbor can only be north, because the west, south, and east neighbors already belong to retained originals. Indeed,  $y$  has exactly one neighbor in its own endpoint set.For a full U, the only endpoints with exactly one own endpoint neighbor are the two leg terminals. All bar endpoints and nonterminal leg endpoints have at least two own neighbors. Thus a U consumer must place a leg terminal at  $y$ .After exchanging the incident and far legs if necessary, its terminal can be taken to be canonical  $(d,1)$ . Its own neighbor must point north, which fixes the canonical row direction and leaves precisely the two stated charts:
$$(r,c)\mapsto(a-1-d+r,C+1-c)$$
and
$$(r,c)\mapsto(a-1-d+r,C-1+c).$$
This is a normalization of the full original data. The leg exchange uses
$$c\mapsto L+1-c$$
and swaps  $d,f$ . For even  $L$ , this reflection preserves the row-zero and row-one matching patterns and exchanges the corresponding original lateral and axial supports. It does not silently replace an immutable matching or support set.The rotor exclusion is also complete. Rotational symmetry identifies the four terminal choices, while reflection gives the two north-terminal forms displayed in the mandatory-footprint note. One contains  $(a-2,C-1)$ , and the other contains  $(a-2,C+1)$ . These are retained P and root/predecessor-V endpoints. Thus neither rotor orientation can be the actual consumer.No dimension cutoff or sampled orientation list is needed for this classification.2. The predecessor X coordinates and the bound in both orientations are correctFor
$$X_{j-1}=U(6,4,4),\qquad
(r,c)\mapsto(a_{j-1}+2-r,s_{j-1}+2-c),$$
the canonical near column  $c=1$  contains endpoints at every canonical row  $r=0,\ldots,4$ . Its image is therefore
$$\{(r,s_{j-1}+1):a_{j-1}-2\le r\le a_{j-1}+2\}.$$
The recurrence gives
$$s_{j-1}+1=C_j,\qquad a_{j-1}=a_j-z_{j-1}+6,$$
so this is exactly
$$\boxed{
\{(r,C_j):a_j-z_{j-1}+4\le r\le a_j-z_{j-1}+8\}.
}$$
Both normalized U frames have the same incident column  $C_j$ , occupied at every row
$$[a_j-1-d,\ a_j-1].$$
Including canonical bar rows zero and one is essential here.Put  $z_-=z_{j-1}$ . Since  $z_-\ge24$ , the entire predecessor segment lies above  $a_j-1$ . Consequently, a consecutive interval ending at  $a_j-1$  can avoid that segment only by starting below its largest row coordinate:
$$a_j-1-d>a_j-z_-+8.$$
Hence
$$d<z_--9,$$
or equivalently for the permitted integer depths,
$$\boxed{d\le z_--10.}$$
This argument is independent of breadth, far depth, and horizontal orientation.For the right frame, canonical lower-bar endpoint  $(1,2)$  maps to
$$(a_j-d,C_j+1).$$
For every even  $4\le d\le z_-$ , this lies in the predecessor V interval
$$[a_j-z_-,a_j]\times\{C_j+1\}.$$
A right owner therefore requires
$$d\ge z_-+2,$$
which contradicts  $d\le z_--10$ .For the left frame, the same canonical endpoint maps to
$$(a_j-d,C_j-1).$$
At  $d=4,6,8$ , it belongs to P’s retained near column. Thus the left frame requires  $d\ge10$ .The asserted necessary classification follows:
$$\boxed{
R_j\text{ is left},\qquad 10\le d\le z_{j-1}-10.
}$$
There is no claim here that every remaining breadth, far depth, or incident depth is feasible. Additional collisions may restrict them further.3. The eleven-point footprint and actual-owner distinctness are soundThe incident column of a left owner with  $d\ge10$  contains
$$[a_j-1-d,\ a_j-1]\times\{C_j\},$$
and therefore contains
$$\boxed{
\{(r,C_j):a_j-11\le r\le a_j-1\}.
}$$
This is eleven endpoints, including both ends. At the limiting depth  $d=10$ , the first one,  $(a_j-11,C_j)$ , is a row-zero bar endpoint. It would be missed by counting only the stem rows  $2,\ldots,d$ ; the submitted argument correctly counts the full column.The distinctness argument also applies to actual originals, not merely to candidate labels.Every E support has checkerboard color
$$(a_j-1)+C_j\equiv 0+1\equiv1\pmod2,$$
and every forced t support has the same color:
$$(a_j-4)+s_j\equiv1+0\equiv1\pmod2.$$
The t-owner terminal assertion can be checked directly from H3. At
$$t_j=(a_j-4,s_j),$$
the retained west, east, and south neighbors are
$$(a_j-4,s_j-1)\in Z_j,\qquad
(a_j-4,s_j+1)\in P_j,\qquad
(a_j-3,s_j)\in Z_j.$$
Thus its actual owner also has exactly one own endpoint neighbor, to the north. Both normalized north-terminal rotor forms contain
$$(a_j-6,s_j+1),$$
which is already a P endpoint. Hence each t owner is also a north-terminal U.The two degree-one terminals of a canonical even U are
$$(d,1),\qquad(f,L),$$
and have opposite checkerboard colors. Lattice isometries preserve whether two sites have equal or opposite color. A single U therefore cannot own two of these forced sites: both would have to be terminals, but the sites have the same color.Finally, the sites are distinct:The t columns  $s_j$  strictly decrease.The E columns satisfy
$$C_j-C_{j+1}=w_j+12>0.$$
A t column is even, while an E column is odd.Thus the  $n$  E owners are mutually distinct and are distinct from all  $n$  t owners. All are fresh relative to H3. This closes the possible owner-reuse issue in the immutable inventory.4. The phase-count consequence uses the correct chargesLet
$$p=\frac{d+f}{2}.$$
For either normalized E frame, the immutable matching count is
$$M=L+p-1.$$
The full physical-tile counts are:E frameEndpoint tilesOriginal supports in those tilesChargeLeft $L/2+p$  $p$  $-1$ Right $L/2+1+p$  $p+4$  $+1$ For the left frame, the bar occupies  $L/2$  tiles, and the legs add  $p$ . The inward odd-row lateral supports contribute  $p-2$  supports inside endpoint tiles; the two terminal axial supports add two.For the right frame, the bar spans  $L/2+1$  tile columns. The even-row lateral supports contribute  $p$  inside supports, the two axial supports contribute two, and the two bar-exterior supports contribute two more.These counts are unaffected by supports being consumed. In particular, the E charge is not  $1-L$ .For completeness, the different t phase—odd terminal row and even terminal column—has the following counts:t frameEndpoint tilesOriginal supports in those tilesChargeLeft $L+p$  $p+2$  $1-L$ Right $L+p-2$  $p-2$  $1-L$ Consequently the new barrier gives
$$n_L\ge n-1,\qquad n_R\le1,$$
and, for the selection of these  $2n$  distinct forced owners relative to H3,
$$\Delta S=\sum_j\bigl(L_j^{(t)}-1\bigr)+n_L,\qquad
\Delta N=n_R.$$
Therefore
$$\boxed{
\Delta(N+S)=\sum_j\bigl(L_j^{(t)}-1\bigr)+n\ge6n.
}$$
The statement “only the first E owner can have positive charge” is correctly restricted to E owners. It neither asserts that a positive first E owner exists nor rules out positive owners elsewhere in a complete extension.This is an exact owner inventory for the specified selection. It does not account for  $2|F|-|E|$ , so it is correctly presented as something short of a net  $\Phi$  bound.5. The refined B interval gap is exact as a necessary conditionWrite
$$a=a_j,\quad s=s_j,\quad z=z_j,\quad v=w_{j+1},\quad C=s+w_j+13.$$
Then
$$a_{j+1}=a+z-6,\qquad s_{j+1}=s-v-12.$$
A right north-terminal  $t_{j+1}$  owner with breadth  $w_j+v+26$ , incident depth  $D$ , and far depth  $g$  has chart
$$(r,c)\mapsto
\bigl(a+z-10-D+r,\ s-v-13+c\bigr).$$
Its far column is
$$s-v-13+(w_j+v+26)=C.$$
Because a full U occupies canonical rows  $0,\ldots,g$  in its far column, including its two bar rows, its complete interval there is
$$I=[a+z-10-D,\ a+z-10-D+g].$$
Both endpoints are odd.Distinctness from  $R_j$ If an endpoint-disjoint candidate B contained
$$y_j=(a-1,C),$$
its interval would also contain  $(a,C)$ : an interval with an odd last row cannot end at the even row  $a-1$ . But  $(a,C)$  is a retained E endpoint.Thus any B disjoint from H3 does not contain  $y_j$ , and consequently cannot be the same actual original as  $R_j$ . This proof does not impose a bound on  $D$  or  $g$ .Avoiding the entire forbidden intervalB must avoid the eleven endpoints of the distinct  $R_j$ , together with the old E endpoint:
$$[a-11,a-1]\cup\{a\}=[a-11,a].$$
A consecutive interval with odd endpoints avoids this block precisely when
$$\max I\le a-12
\quad\text{or}\quad
\min I\ge a+2.$$
Substituting the endpoints of  $I$  gives
$$\boxed{
D-g\ge z+2
\quad\text{or}\quad
D\le z-12.
}$$
So the refinement from the earlier nine-point condition is correct. In the deep alternative,
$$D\ge z+2+g\ge z+6.$$
If  $D=z+6$ , then  $g\le4$ , and hence  $g=4$ .For  $D=z+4$ , the interval starts at  $a-14$ , and every  $g\ge4$  makes it contain
$$(a-10,C).$$
That point belongs to the eleven-point footprint. Thus the exclusion holds for every permitted even far depth, not merely for the smallest choice.The dichotomy is exact for avoidance of this particular forbidden interval. It remains only a necessary condition for a complete extension, as the note expressly states.6. The explicit example is disjoint from all of H3The recurrence produces

(a_2,s_2)=(67,-48).$$

$$a=49,\qquad C=1.$$

It does not meet B. Thus the example is disjoint from the full H3 inventory, including its P repairs, west rotors, X originals, and root.Nevertheless, any complete extension must contain an internal E owner  $R_1$  whose endpoint set includes

B contains  $(39,1)$ —indeed both  $(38,1)$  and  $(39,1)$ —but does not contain  $y_1=(48,1)$ . Hence B and  $R_1$  are distinct and would share endpoints.Therefore

This conclusion follows from an explicit forced collision. It does not depend on a finite search failing to find an extension.7. The first-root theorem and conditional additivity remain intactThe additional restriction is genuinely specific to internal indices. The first root has no retained predecessor  $X_{-1}$ , so the new upper bound on incident depth is unavailable there.The coordinate distinction is particularly clear for the first-deep choice  $D=z+4,g=4$ . Its far-column interval is
$$[a-14,a-10].$$
At the first root, the earlier universal E footprint begins at  $a-9$ , so those intervals do not force a collision. The accepted right E owner of depth  $8$  has exactly that incident starting row.At an internal root, the predecessor barrier forces the left phase and incident depth at least  $10$ . The mandatory footprint then begins at  $a-11$ , and the same B interval necessarily intersects it.Thus there are two relevant failures of an attempted internal clone:The first-root right E phase cannot be made into an internal actual E owner merely by choosing a different incident depth: the V lower bound and X upper bound are incompatible for every right depth.Even the first-deep B candidate, which can remain disjoint from all old H3 endpoints, cannot coexist with the actual E owner that completeness forces.Neither conclusion changes a valid receipt identity for a partial selected union.Conditional additivity also remains unaffected. When distinct added originals have genuinely disjoint affected physical-tile footprints and each source charge is counted once, their new increments can be added under those hypotheses. The present theorem shows that the proposed internal clone cannot supply an actual instance in a complete extension. It does not falsify the accounting statement.The note therefore maintains the correct scope: it proves necessary internal-owner geometry, an exact immutable phase inventory, and a nonextendibility obstruction for a specified partial family. It establishes neither a complete extension in the surviving phases nor a full-family allocation, and it gives no counterexample to the global inequality.
